extracted.intended_audience: authors and reviewers submitting to or reviewing for Nature Geoscience (and the broader geoscience research community)
extracted.subtask_description: Journal policy describing how Nature Geoscience will implement transparent peer review (TPR): who is eligible, what reviewer–author material will be published, timing and opt-in rules, reviewer anonymity/recognition, and redaction/exclusion rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility by article type and submission date
rubrics_metrics.description: The TPR option will be available to authors of Article, Analysis, or Brief Communication manuscripts first sent for peer review from 19 August 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies specifically to those manuscript types and only to manuscripts first sent for peer review on or after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author opt-in timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will be able to opt in before their paper is accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The choice to publish reviewer reports and responses must be made by the authors prior to acceptance; opt-in is not described as reversible after acceptance in this statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published content: reviewer reports and author responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer reports and author responses will be published online with the paper as a supplementary peer review file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The peer review file will accompany the published paper as a supplementary file; the policy explicitly refers to the text of reports submitted as documents and author response text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction policy for confidential or third-party content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer–author exchanges will only be edited to redact content that is confidential or owned by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only redactions for confidentiality or third-party ownership will be made; otherwise reviewer reports/responses are published as provided (subject to the marked-up manuscript exclusion below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for reviewer–author exchanges transferred from other journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer–author exchanges for another journal that are transferred to us with the associated manuscript will not be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission arrives with peer review correspondence from another journal, those exchanged reports/responses will not be published as part of Nature Geoscience's peer review file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion when Nature Geoscience correspondence is transferred away
rubrics_metrics.description: When manuscripts we considered for publication are subsequently transferred and published by another journal in the Nature Portfolio with a TPR policy, no Nature Geoscience correspondence will be included in the peer review file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the manuscript is moved away to another Nature Portfolio journal that publishes TPR, Nature Geoscience's internal correspondence will not be carried into that journal's peer review file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer notification at invitation and inability to opt out
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will be given information about TPR when they are invited to review. They will not be able to opt out; rather, it is up to the authors whether they want to opt in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are informed up-front that reports may be published under the journal's TPR option; however, reviewers cannot unilaterally prevent publication of their report if authors opt in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity and signing option
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will remain anonymous unless they decide to sign their reports, and in all other respects, our confidentiality policy is unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is anonymity; reviewers may choose to be named by signing their report. The general confidentiality protections of the journal continue to apply beyond the TPR policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recognition mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can still be recognized for their contribution by consenting to be named in the reviewer recognition statement on submission of their report, or by the options specified on our website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate mechanisms (reviewer recognition statement and other website options) allow reviewers to receive credit if they consent; these operate alongside the TPR publication of reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked-up manuscripts not included / not accepted from reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: While we can include the text of reports submitted as a document in the peer review file, we cannot include marked-up manuscripts, and so we are no longer accepting these from reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only textual reports (and author responses) are suitable for publication in the peer review file; reviewers should not submit annotated/marked-up manuscript files because these will not be published and are no longer accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and benefits of publishing reviewer–author exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal encourages publication of reviewer–author exchanges because they demonstrate how the review process improves clarity and robustness, show the efforts reviewers and authors make, and may inform specialists, early-career researchers, and non-specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPR is presented as improving transparency and as an educational resource: it can reveal alternative methods/hypotheses tested, show expectations of reviewers, and clarify contributions and implications for various audiences.
